# Install on Linux

Start here if you have never installed Neovim, Homebrew, or a terminal development tool. Follow the steps in order. No GitHub or AI account is needed for the local practice workspace.

[Interactive guide / Panduan interaktif](https://ardanngrha.github.io/vimdesk/?lang=en&os=linux#install)

Ubuntu/Debian with Bash and Homebrew. Start with a supported 64-bit distribution; Ubuntu 24.04 or newer is a practical starting point. These instructions were checked against official documentation, but VimDesk has not been tested end to end on Linux.

Requires Neovim 0.12+ and Python 3.9+.

## 1. Open a Linux terminal

Open your distribution's Terminal app. On Ubuntu, Ctrl + Alt + T usually opens it. This walkthrough uses Bash. Paste commands with Ctrl + Shift + V, then press Enter; copy the commands without a $ prompt.

**Terminal**

```sh
cat /etc/os-release
uname -m
echo "$SHELL"
```

**Success check:** You can identify the distribution and architecture. Use a regular user with sudo access, not a root login. The commands below are for Ubuntu/Debian.

> For Fedora, Arch, or another distribution, use its own development-tool installation commands from the Homebrew on Linux reference. Check Homebrew's architecture and system requirements before continuing.

## 2. Install Linux build tools

Run these commands in the Ubuntu/Debian terminal, including when using Ubuntu in WSL. sudo may ask for your Linux user's password. The password does not appear while typing. These packages provide Git, downloads, Python, and the compiler needed for plugin parsers.

**Terminal**

```sh
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y build-essential procps curl file git ca-certificates python3 unzip
```

**Terminal**

```sh
git --version
python3 --version
cc --version
```

**Success check:** Installation finishes and each check prints a version. Wait for the terminal prompt before continuing.

> These apt commands do not apply to Fedora or Arch. If sudo is unavailable or your account cannot install packages, ask the machine's administrator to install the prerequisites.

## 3. Install Homebrew inside Linux

This guide uses Homebrew to obtain the required Neovim and tool versions. Run the official installer as your regular Linux user and follow its prompts. In WSL, run it inside Ubuntu, not PowerShell. If brew already exists and works, skip its installation.

**Terminal**

```sh
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
```

**Terminal: For the standard Linux prefix and Bash**

```sh
eval "$(/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
printf '\neval "$(/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew shellenv)"\n' >> "$HOME/.bashrc"
brew --version
```

**Success check:** brew prints a version. Follow the installer's exact Next steps if its prefix or shell differs from this example.

> Add shellenv only once. For zsh use ~/.zshrc instead of ~/.bashrc. Do not run brew or the VimDesk installer with sudo. A distribution's older Neovim package may not meet VimDesk's minimum version.

## 4. Install Neovim and the core tools

Install the editor, Git UI, file-search tools, Python, and parser builder. These are the apps the workbench uses. Wait until Homebrew returns to the Terminal prompt.

**Terminal**

```sh
brew install neovim git lazygit ripgrep fd python tree-sitter
```

**Terminal: Check the installed tools**

```sh
nvim --version
git --version
lazygit --version
rg --version
fd --version
python3 --version
tree-sitter --version
```

**Success check:** Neovim is 0.12 or newer, Python is 3.9 or newer, and tree-sitter is at least 0.26.1. Each other command prints a version instead of “command not found”.

> If Neovim was already installed but is too old, run brew upgrade neovim. Do the same for an outdated python or tree-sitter formula. You do not need to upgrade every app on the Mac.

## 5. Download and install the workbench

Neovim is the editor; this repository adds its interface and workflow. The commands create a Developer folder in your home directory, download the source, check dependencies, and install a separate workbench profile. No GitHub account is needed to download it.

**Terminal**

```sh
mkdir -p "$HOME/Developer"
cd "$HOME/Developer"
git clone https://github.com/ardanngrha/vimdesk.git
cd vimdesk
./install.sh doctor
./install.sh
```

**Success check:** The installer prints Installed, Backup, and Launch. Its default config is ~/.config/vimdesk and its launcher is ~/.local/bin/vimdesk. Your existing ~/.config/nvim is preserved.

> Doctor’s [--] next to a language server, codex, or claude is optional. Missing core tools or an unsupported Neovim version must be fixed first. If the checkout folder already exists, use the update instructions below; do not delete your existing folder.

## 6. Open a two-repo practice workspace

A repository (repo) is a project folder whose history is tracked with Git. From the vimdesk source folder, run the demo below. It creates a new temporary folder with backend and frontend Git repositories, then opens your installed workbench. Each repo has a small change to review.

**Terminal**

```sh
./scripts/demo.sh
```

**Success check:** Neovim opens and lazy.nvim may download plugins on its first run. Wait for downloads to finish. If the plugin window stays open after completion, press q to close it.

> The practice repositories are local only: no remote, GitHub login, push, or real project is involved. Their temporary path is printed in Terminal and may be cleaned by the operating system later. Keep important work in your own project folder.

## 7. Finish plugins and syntax highlighting

The following commands go inside Neovim, not Terminal. Press Esc first, type the command including its leading colon, then Enter. Restore the locked plugin versions and wait until it finishes. Quit with :qa, then run ./scripts/demo.sh again in Terminal to restart.

**Inside Neovim**

```vim
:Lazy restore
```

**Inside Neovim: After restarting Neovim**

```vim
:WorkbenchParsers
```

**Inside Neovim: Check the workbench**

```vim
:WorkbenchDoctor
```

**Success check:** Parser downloads and compilation complete, then source files gain syntax highlighting. :messages shows parser progress/errors. Doctor lists installed tools. Optional language servers can still be missing.

> Do not close Neovim while parsers are compiling. If installation fails, check internet, cc --version and tree-sitter --version in Terminal, then retry :WorkbenchParsers.

## 8. Try your first edit, review and quit

Press Space, release it, then g, then Shift + g. The Git sidebar should list backend and frontend. Click a repo name to show its Changes, then a changed file to see Before / After. Click the branch badge beside a repo to choose a branch; commit or stash changes before switching. Graph below Changes lets you expand commits and review their files. For editing, open a file from Files, press i to type, then Esc to return to Normal mode.

**Inside Neovim: Save the current file**

```vim
:w
```

**Inside Neovim: Quit all windows**

```vim
:qa
```

**Success check:** The file saves with :w. :qa exits when no changes are pending. If there are unsaved edits, save first or use Space q q for a confirmation prompt. Press u in Normal mode to undo; Ctrl + r redoes.

> Space shortcuts are sequential, not simultaneous. Ctrl means Control, not Command. Inside LazyGit, q exits that Git view; press ? there to see its own bindings.

## 9. Add the launcher to Bash and open projects

After quitting Neovim, run these commands in the same Linux or Ubuntu terminal. PATH tells the shell where to find programs. Add the launcher's folder once so vimdesk works by name in new Bash sessions.

**Terminal**

```sh
printf '\nexport PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"\n' >> "$HOME/.bashrc"
source "$HOME/.bashrc"
command -v vimdesk
```

**Terminal**

```sh
vimdesk "$HOME/Developer"
```

**Success check:** command -v prints ~/.local/bin/vimdesk's full path and Neovim opens your parent workspace. Opening a single repository also works.

> For zsh use ~/.zshrc. In Windows, reopen the Ubuntu profile to run VimDesk; it is not a PowerShell command. Clipboard integration depends on the terminal and Linux display environment; see the platform notes below if copying between Neovim and other apps fails.

## Platform notes

For desktop clipboard integration, install wl-clipboard for Wayland or xclip for X11 using your distribution's package manager. Run :checkhealth vim.provider if copying between Neovim and other apps fails. Terminal text selection/copy is separate from Neovim registers. The optional Homebrew language-server helper below also runs inside Linux.

## Files, preview tabs and icons

Single-click a file to preview it. Double-click, press Enter, or start editing to keep its tab. Open Editors lists existing buffers. The six toolbar icons, from left to right, are New File, New Folder, More, Collapse All, Reveal Active File and Paste. More opens the named actions menu.

File icons need a Nerd Font, such as Hack Nerd Font Mono, selected in your terminal settings. [Download a font from Nerd Fonts](https://www.nerdfonts.com/font-downloads), install it using your OS font installer, and select it in the terminal. For WSL, install/select the font on Windows in the Windows Terminal profile, not inside Ubuntu. On Linux, use your desktop font installer or ~/.local/share/fonts. Restart the terminal if the new font is not listed. Fonts are not bundled with VimDesk.

Press Space, then u, then i to toggle file icons; Space b p keeps a preview; Space u p toggles Light mode. Light mode disables explorer watchers and decorations; use u in Files or r in Git to refresh. It does not unload language servers or cap their RAM.

[Files and settings / Files dan pengaturan](workflow.md#preview-tabs-and-open-editors)

## Review and stage Git changes

Select a repo in Git. The Changes heading offers Open All, Discard All and Stage All; a narrow sidebar shows [Open] [↶] [+]. Beside each working file, [↶] discards that file and [+] stages it. [−] unstages a staged file. Save your edits before staging.

Open All shows files one after another in a read-only Before / After view. Click a file heading to fold it, use [f / ]f to jump between files, and click Open to edit the real file. Enter opens an individual diff; Refresh reloads snapshots. Space g c closes the review. Individual working-file diffs and merge Result remain editable.

Discard asks for confirmation and saves a recovery copy, while preserving staged changes. To recover the latest batch for the selected repo, use More → Restore last discard. Recovery refuses to overwrite newer edits or a changed index; its backup path is in Git Log. Review the files before committing or discarding.

[Git review and recovery / Review Git dan pemulihan](workflow.md#review-and-resolve-conflicts)

## Optional: language support and AI

For completion, diagnostics and formatting, install language servers from the source checkout:

```sh
cd "$HOME/Developer/vimdesk"
./scripts/dependencies.sh languages
```

This installs servers for Go, JavaScript/TypeScript/React, Rust and Python. Projects still need their own runtimes and dependencies. Use a project-compatible Go toolchain, a Rust toolchain with Clippy, Node.js for JS/TS, and the project’s Python/venv. Follow the project’s setup instructions; the workbench does not install project packages for you.

AI is optional. Install and authenticate [Codex CLI](https://github.com/openai/codex) or [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) using their official guides. Save files, stage the changes, click Generate in Git, select an agent, and review the subject before clicking Commit. The staged diff is sent to the selected provider using your account. Normal usage limits/costs apply.

The practice repos have no remotes. For real projects, configure a remote and authenticate with that Git hosting provider before pushing. Git commit identity and remote login are different settings. See [GitHub’s first-time Git setup](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/git-basics/set-up-git).

## If something goes wrong

- **brew: command not found:** Run the exact Next steps printed by the Homebrew installer, then reopen Terminal.
- **destination path already exists:** The source was already downloaded. Use cd "$HOME/Developer/vimdesk", then git pull --ff-only and ./install.sh. Back up local edits first.
- **vimdesk: command not found:** Use ~/.local/bin/vimdesk, or complete the final step to add the launcher to PATH. In Windows, use the Ubuntu terminal.
- **Cannot type / tidak bisa mengetik:** Press i to enter Insert mode. Press Esc to return to Normal mode before shortcuts or colon commands.
- **No completion / tidak ada completion:** LSP servers are optional. Install the relevant server and project runtime, open an actual source file, then run :checkhealth vim.lsp.
- **No author identity / identitas commit belum ada:** For your own repo, configure user.name and user.email following your Git provider’s guide. The demo supplies its own local fixture identity only.
